name: Bitwise Queries (Hard Version)
description:
The only difference between the easy and hard versions is the constraints on the number of queries. This is an interactive problem. Ridbit has a hidden array $$$a$$$ of $$$n$$$ integers which he wants Ashish to guess. Note that $$$n$$$ is a power of two . Ashish is allowed to ask three different types of queries. They are of the form AND $$$i$$$ $$$j$$$: ask for the bitwise AND of elements $$$a_i$$$ and $$$a_j$$$ $$$(1 \leq i, j \le n$$$, $$$i 
eq j)$$$ OR $$$i$$$ $$$j$$$: ask for the bitwise OR of elements $$$a_i$$$ and $$$a_j$$$ $$$(1 \leq i, j \le n$$$, $$$i 
eq j)$$$ XOR $$$i$$$ $$$j$$$: ask for the bitwise XOR of elements $$$a_i$$$ and $$$a_j$$$ $$$(1 \leq i, j \le n$$$, $$$i 
eq j)$$$ Can you help Ashish guess the elements of the array? In this version, each element takes a value in the range $$$[0, n-1]$$$ (inclusive) and Ashish can ask no more than $$$n+1$$$ queries.
input_specification: The first line of input contains one integer $$$n$$$ $$$(4 \le n \le 2^{16})$$$ — the length of the array. It is guaranteed that $$$n$$$ is a power of two .
approach_summary: Design an adaptive query strategy maintaining uncertainty bounds. Halve candidate space or probe tree centroids using at most the allowed query budget.
